# THEORYs with `tags` `learning-theory`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Learning theory** — why learning generalizes and how it proceeds — compression and description length, Kolmogorov complexity and sufficient statistics, rate–distortion and PAC-style bounds, model selection; and training dynamics: solvable models of learning trajectories, stages, plateaus and phase transitions in training, and the implicit bias of optimisation. A work whose subject is how to train a model better is ML practice and goes to the anthology (ADR-036).

| [THEORY-028](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-028.md) v2 | Generalisation error ≤ √(2σ²·I) | Russo & Zou (2015), [LIT-356](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-356.md), Prop. 1: \|E[φ_T − µ_T]\| ≤ σ√(2·I(T;φ)) for any selection T among σ-sub-Gaussian statistics. Both proofs rest on Donsker–Varadhan and were checked by the readers. The bound is in expectation only. | [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v4 | Landauer prices only losing distinguishability | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit exported to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom, which "need not" be heat. The record derives it for a memory and environment evolving reversibly from an uncorrelated start: the environment's entropy rises by at least the logical entropy lost, H(X \| f(X)), and an injective step has no floor, attained exactly by a permutation. Goldt & Seifert ([LIT-308](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-308.md)) bound information learnt by total entropy production, payable with vanishing heat in their toy model. It does not license a k_BT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, per gradient step or per bit learnt. Whether the bound survives without reversible dynamics is [QUESTION-215](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-215.md). | Active |

This gives the steps–examples hyperbola and B_crit = E_min/S_min. The Hessian-free B_simple = tr(Σ)/\|G\|² is the batch at which gradient noise equals signal, and it tracks B_crit within about 10× on most of eight tasks, missing by about 20× on two generative models. The authors call the derivation one with "unfounded assumptions". Nothing in it is information-theoretic, and its temperature ε/B is not k_BT. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md) v2 | Top Fisher eigenvalues span the class means | Papyan (2019), [LIT-619](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-619.md): for softmax cross-entropy the Gauss–Newton matrix G, which is the model's Fisher averaged over inputs, is an uncentred second moment of logit derivatives indexed by class and logit. It decomposes exactly into four terms (Eq. 28), and its top C eigenvalues match those of the class-mean term G₁. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), splits those C into one global-mean outlier and C − 1 between-class ones, finds a C(C − 1) cross-class mini-bulk beneath them, and proves the whole pattern for a Gaussian toy model. Papyan (2018), [LIT-617](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-617.md), supplies the measurements and the attribution of the Hessian's outliers to G. The decomposition is algebra. That G₁ carries the outliers is measured, by eye, under a training protocol narrower than practice. So this is Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-079](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-079.md) v3 | Laplace BMR misprices singular reductions | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. BMR's closed form (Friston & Penny, [LIT-620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-620.md), Eq. 9; Friston, Parr & Zeidman, [LIT-614](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-614.md), Eq. 11) charges a reduction through log-determinants of Gaussian precisions, which is MacKay's regular Occam factor. Watanabe, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), says that models with hierarchical layers or hidden variables are singular, that no normal distribution approximates their posterior, and that their free energy grows as λ log n. BMR is applied to exactly such models: mixtures, hierarchical empirical Bayes and latent states. Neither literature cites the other. The exact identity is untouched ([THEORY-081](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-081.md)). The claim is about its Laplace form, and a test on reduced-rank regression would settle it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-080](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-080.md) v4 | NTK eigenvalues schedule the Occam penalty | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. Its exact half is filed as the record's own claim, CLAIM-384; what stays here is the spherical account. A network linearised at initialisation, with an isotropic Gaussian prior on its parameters and Gaussian noise, is MacKay's linear-in-parameters model ([LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md)). Its Occam factor is −½ Σ log(1 + βλ_a/α) over the eigenvalues of JᵀJ. These are the empirical NTK's, which on uniform spherical data form Bietti & Bach's degree blocks, nµ_k with multiplicity N(d, k) ([LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md)). Degrees whose βnµ_k exceeds α pay about ½ log n per harmonic, and degrees below pay almost nothing. With µ_k ~ k^(−d), the number of paid directions γ grows as n^((d−1)/d), not as the parameter count. Basri et al.'s bound ([LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), Eq. 14) is the matching data-fit term. The kernel's decay exponent is the schedule of the penalty. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-082.md) | Natural-gradient efficiency needs full-rank Fisher | Amari (1998), [LIT-607](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-607.md). Theorem 1 is a Lagrangian derivation: under \|dw\|² = Σg_ij dw_i dw_j the steepest-descent direction is −G⁻¹∇L, so it changes with G. Theorem 2 shows that online learning with step 1/t along the Fisher natural gradient attains the Cramér–Rao bound G⁻¹/t, and its proof uses G(w*)⁻¹. Watanabe, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), Eq. 14, calls a truth regular when the optimum is one point and its Fisher is positive definite, and singular otherwise. From Amari's own Eq. 6.12, the score for hidden unit i's input weights carries the factor v_i. So the Fisher of a multilayer perceptron loses rank wherever an output weight is zero. That set is part of the optimum whenever the teacher needs fewer hidden units than the student has. Active because each step is checkable in the two texts. The claim that the Fisher is the only invariant metric is Chentsov's, cited and not held. | Active |
| [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md) v4 | Neural collapse forms, only partly on ImageNet | Papyan, Han & Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), measured 480 trained classifiers on seven datasets with VGG, ResNet and DenseNet. Through the terminal phase, within-class variability of last-layer features falls (NC1), and the centred class means become equinorm and equiangular with cosine −1/(C − 1) (NC2). The classifier aligns with them (NC3), and the decision becomes nearest class mean (NC4). They prove that NC1 and NC2 imply NC3 and NC4 for the MSE-optimal and max-margin classifiers, and that the simplex ETF is the unique error-exponent-optimal codebook. Read from the plots, collapse is close to complete on the four easier datasets and partial on ImageNet at the last epoch. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), sees class means separate and grow more orthogonal with depth. The measurements cover one protocol, and the dynamics are unexplained outside free-features models. Within them, THEORY-278 (LIT-974) derives collapse for MSE under a re-whitened flow, and THEORY-286 (LIT-994) gives the cross-entropy endpoint under class imbalance. The paper's further claim, that the Hessian's class outliers are a symptom of collapse, is argued and not measured, and is left to [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md) v4 | Lazy Fisher inherits NTK harmonic blocks | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. The identity is linear algebra: JᵀJ (parameters × parameters) and JJᵀ (samples × samples) have the same non-zero eigenvalues. Under squared loss JᵀJ is the Gauss–Newton matrix and the Fisher. JJᵀ is the empirical NTK Gram matrix, which in the kernel regime on uniform spherical data has the degree-block spectrum of Bietti & Bach (2021), [LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md): µ_k with multiplicity N(d, k). The threshold claim draws on Cao et al. (2019), [LIT-624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-624.md). Their guarantees are stated only for whole eigenspaces, with sample costs that grow as the gap below them shrinks. It also draws on Basri et al. (2019), [LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), where a structural zero block shows up in a finite sample as small non-zero eigenvalues. No paper filed computes a Fisher spectrum in this regime. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-085](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-085.md) v2 | K-FAC misplaces cross-class Fisher pairings | Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md): per layer, the Fisher is a weighted sum of Kronecker products of features and backpropagated errors (Eq. 7.5), and its class outliers come from class means of gradients that are approximately h_c ⊗ δ_c. K-FAC (Martens & Grosse 2015, [LIT-622](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-622.md)) multiplies the class-averaged feature covariance by the class-averaged error covariance. Papyan finds its outliers and mini-bulks "drastically misaligned", and the class-wise CFAC aligns much better at deep layers. The identity relating the two, CFAC − K-FAC = the class-weighted between-class covariance of the factors, is the record's own and is filed as CLAIM-391. The evidence for the mechanism is one MLP, spectra only, judged by eye. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-086](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-086.md) v2 | NTK fits eigenspaces at eigenvalue-set rates | Three derived results that compose. Cao et al. (2019), [LIT-624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-624.md), Theorem 4.2: for a wide two-layer ReLU network, the training residual's component in the top-r_k NTK eigenspace falls as (1 − λ_{r_k})^T, for any target. Basri et al. (2019), [LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md): on uniform spherical data the Gram matrix is a convolution, so its eigenvectors are harmonics, with closed-form eigenvalues per frequency. The bias-free kernel is zero on odd frequencies k ≥ 3, and a bias restores them. Bietti & Bach (2021), [LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md), Corollary 3: the L-layer ReLU NTK decays as k^(−d) on S^(d−1), the same exponent at every depth. Active for the kernel regime on uniform spherical data, where every step is proved. It says nothing about networks whose kernel moves. | Active |
| [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md) v4 | Singular models pay λ log n, below d/2 | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), writes the evidence as best-fit likelihood times an Occam factor, the ratio of posterior to prior accessible volume, which under a Gaussian approximation is P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A. When the likelihood dominates, det A grows as n^d, so the penalty is (d/2) log n. Watanabe's WBIC paper, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), recovers that case (Lemma 3, Theorem 5) and states what replaces it when the Fisher information is degenerate at the optimum: λ log n − (m − 1) log log n, with λ the RLCT (Theorem 2). The regular half is re-derived by Laplace's method with its conditions. The singular half is Watanabe's cited theorem, checked by exact free energies in two singular models of known λ. The volume reading of λ is in Watanabe's book, which is unread. | Active |

| [THEORY-106](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-106.md) | Ridge removes the double-descent peak | Liao, Couillet & Mahoney (2020), [LIT-679](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-679.md): for random Fourier features with n, p and N large together, the test MSE has a closed form through a deterministic equivalent of the resolvent. As λ → 0 its corrections jump from O(1) to order 1/λ across 2N = n, det(Ω⁻¹) scales as λ, and the test error diverges at 2N = n unless the test data lie within about λ of the training data. At λ = 10⁻⁷ and 10⁻³ the curve has a singular peak; at the tuned λ ≈ 0.2 and at 10 it has none. Dereziński, Liang & Mahoney (2019), [LIT-683](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-683.md): exact MSE of the minimum-norm estimator under a surrogate design, peaking at n = d with value σ² tr(Σ⁻¹), and below the threshold equal in expectation to ridge regression at the λn that makes the ridge effective dimension n. Proportional-limit theorems for one shallow model each; nothing here reaches trained deep networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-108](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-108.md) | Connectivity, not flatness, predicts accuracy | Yang, Hodgkinson, Theisen, Zou, Gonzalez, Ramchandran & Mahoney (2021), [LIT-663](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-663.md): thousands of trained networks on a load by temperature grid, measured by the endpoint Hessian, by mode connectivity on a trained Bezier curve between two independent runs, and by CKA of their outputs. Phases III (flat, poorly connected) and IV-A (flat, connected) have almost the same Hessian and different accuracy; with 10% noisy labels the sharp, unconverged phases beat phase III; label noise barely moves the Hessian while connectivity and CKA fall. The best accuracy is in the flat, connected, high-similarity phase IV-B. The counterexamples are to the anthology's [ANTH-SOTA-012](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/practices.d/SOTA-012.md). One architecture family carries most of it, phases are read by eye, and connectivity alone also fails when the load is data amount. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md) v4 | Pair coverage, not data volume, drives composition | Uselis, Dittadi & Oh (2025), [LIT-667](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-667.md). In an n × n grid of two concepts with k combinations seen per value, ResNet-50s trained from scratch fit seen pairs and fail on unseen ones; four times the data of the same combinations leaves 60–80% drops, while more values and more combinations help. Features pass from spurious, to decodable but entangled, to linearly factored as coverage grows. Model selection was on the test set, by design, so the results bound what is possible. The record re-derived that exactly factored embeddings of every unseen pair are fixed by seen pairs connecting every value, as the paper's k = 2 cycle does. Honest selection, other architectures and more concepts are [QUESTION-207](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-207.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-169.md) v3 | In-context conditioning is training, in kind | Sun et al. (2024), [LIT-801](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-801.md), Theorems 1–2, with von Oswald et al. (2022), [LIT-792](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-792.md), Proposition 1. Linear attention equals a layer whose state is a linear model's weights, updated by batch gradient descent on the context from zero; softmax attention equals a Nadaraya–Watson learner whose "training" appends the context to a list; and, with constructed weights, one linear attention layer reproduces one gradient step of a linear regression on in-context pairs. These are identities of output for specific layers. They do not say that trained transformers do gradient descent (the anthology rejects that, [ANTH-THEORY-068](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/theory.d/THEORY-068.md)), nor anything about weight updates that persist across sequences. | Active |

Measured on TinyStories and WikiText-103, with transformers up to about 10^8 tokens and horizons of tens of tokens, the fitted exponent overlaps γ/(2β), best near the start of the envelope; γ is estimated from trained models' own n-gram losses. Whether the horizon is why is open (QUESTION-233). | Active |
| [THEORY-206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-206.md) v3 | Flattening monomials costs exponential neurons | Rolnick and Tegmark (2017), [LIT-890](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-890.md), Theorems 4.1 to 4.3, extending Lin, Tegmark and Rolnick's 2ⁿ for a product ([LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md)). Proved for Taylor matching at the origin with bias-free units; the uniform version's lower bound rests on an unproved step. The flip side, that a polynomial of degree d with c monomials costs one layer at most c·2ᵈ however many inputs it has, is the edge: the separation does not reach the low-order polynomials [LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md) calls natural. | Active |
| [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md) v2 | Converged SGD samples a modified Gibbs law | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md). Modelled as an underdamped Langevin equation with noise covariance proportional to the Hessian, SGD at the end of training converges to a nonequilibrium stationary state: Gibbs on a modified loss whose curvature undoes the Hessian's anisotropy, with inverse temperature S(1 − β²), in broken detailed balance. A ResNet-18 on ImageNet explores isotropically in a plane where the loss is anisotropic, oscillates at Hessian-dependent rates, and moves at the predicted speed across a hyperparameter sweep. For the learned-structure line, a trained solution is in part a property of the regime that trained it. Proposed: the deep-learning evidence is one network, under assumptions the paper concedes are strained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-210](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-210.md) v2 | Init and optimizer set position on symmetry orbits | Zhao, Walters & Yu (2025), [LIT-970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-970.md), read in [NOTE-712](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-712.md): a survey, so the dynamical results are secondhand. Continuous parameter-space symmetries (GL, scaling, orthogonal, translation) make minima positive-dimensional and connected, which is one source of mode connectivity. Under gradient flow each gives a conserved quantity, such as layer imbalance, that is fixed by initialization and locates the endpoint on the manifold. Under SGD these are not conserved. Read first-hand (Neural Mechanics; Ziyin et al.), weight decay drives the conserved quantities toward zero, and minibatch noise drives a rescaling symmetry's toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances. The survey had reported this as imbalance decaying with large learning rates, and a stationary distribution biased toward balanced solutions that a Langevin model does not predict. This is the null-space half that [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)'s limiting dynamics leave out. Proposed: one survey, with the SGD results unread here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md) v5 | SGD noise equalizes noise across symmetric groups | Ziyin, Li & Ueda ([LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md)), with the gradient flow conservation law and the Itô term from Neural Mechanics ([LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md)). If ℓ(u, w) = ℓ(λu, w/λ) for every sample, then under the SDE model of SGD d(‖u‖² − ‖w‖²)/dt = −T(uᵀC₁u − wᵀC₂w), with T = η/S. The noise has no component along the symmetry, but its dependence on the parameters produces a deterministic drift through Itô's lemma. The drift points to the noise-balanced point, and weight decay adds to its rate. In a diagonal linear network the stationary distribution follows exactly: it is non-ergodic, has a memory of initialization, and collapses to zero above a critical temperature. The law is re-derived here (2026-10-19) within the SDE model; the tests are small synthetic networks, and whether it holds in deep networks on real data is QUESTION-164. | Active |
| [THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md) v3 | Layer balance sets rich versus lazy learning | Dominé et al. (2025), [LIT-943](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-943.md), read in [NOTE-715](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-715.md). With whitened inputs and a λ-balanced start, W₂ᵀW₂ − W₁W₁ᵀ = λI, the full gradient flow is solved exactly. λ is conserved and sets the regime. As λ → 0, singular values are learned in sigmoidal stages, as in Saxe et al., and both layers become task-specific. As \|λ\| → ∞, learning is exponential, the NTK is static, and the larger layer stays near the identity while the smaller carries the task at scale ∝ 1/\|λ\|. The paper analyses gradient flow only. Under SGD the conserved quantity drifts ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md)), which [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) takes up. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-213.md) v4 | Weight decay puts minima on mirror subspaces | Ziyin (2024), [LIT-1014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1014.md), read in [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md). If a per-sample loss is invariant under the reflection I − 2OOᵀ, then Oᵀθ = 0 is a stationary condition for GD and SGD. The Hessian is block diagonal there. Above a critical weight decay all minima satisfy the constraint. Under SGD with strong noise the subspace is attractive even at a strict saddle, by a Lyapunov-exponent argument. Rescaling, rotation and permutation symmetries imply mirrors, so they yield sparsity, low rank and merged neurons, with collapse and loss of plasticity as consequences. The SGD half is approximate and the network evidence is limited; the title holds only the exact half. Promoted on 2026-10-20 on the exact half, re-derived. The SGD half is QUESTION-206. | Active |
| [THEORY-228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-228.md) v3 | Probe error bounded by augmentation conductance | HaoChen, Wei, Gaidon & Ma (2021), [LIT-249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-249.md), read in [NOTE-740](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-740.md). On a finite augmentation space, with labels recoverable from augmentations up to error α and k ≥ 2r, every population minimizer of the spectral contrastive loss has linear-probe error Õ(α/ρ²_⌊k/2⌋), where ρ is the sparsest-partition conductance of the augmentation graph (Thm 3.8). The guarantee needs no conditional independence of the views given the label. It is a statement about the population optimum of one loss: it says nothing about what training reaches, nothing about InfoNCE, and its infinite-space extension is asserted, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md) v4 | Barlow Twins learns eigenvectors in order | Simon et al. (2023), [LIT-242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md), read in [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md). For L = ‖C − I‖²_F with λ = 1, no batch norm and C symmetrized by hand, a linear model from aligned initialization learns mode j at τ_j ≈ −log(s_j(0)²γ_j)/(8γ_j) (Prop. 4.1, proved), the top spectral solutions are exactly the minimum-norm zero-loss ones (Prop. 4.3), and the kernel version is kernel PCA on K_Γ (Prop. 5.1). Generic small initialization is covered by an informal derivation only. The operator is built from the model's kernel and the sample pairs, not from the positive-pair density ratio, and the stepwise growth seen in ResNets under SimCLR and VICReg is an experiment, not a consequence. | Active |
| [THEORY-238](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-238.md) v4 | Encoder alone bounds generalization error | Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski (2023), [LIT-245](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-245.md), read in [NOTE-742](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-742.md). Theorem 4: E[gen] ≤ inf 2√((2·MDL + K + 2)/n) + ε, where MDL is the expected KL of the joint law of the latents of the training set and an independent ghost set to any prior invariant under label-preserving permutations, and ε is the distortion allowed by lossy compression. It holds for any decoder. With a product prior it reduces to sample-wise mutual information. The bound is never evaluated, the prior may depend on unseen ghost data, and a 2√((K+2)/n) floor remains. It does not prove that I(X;U) cannot bound generalization. | Active |
| [THEORY-239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md) v3 | Top singular functions minimize probe error | Zhai (2025), [LIT-975](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-975.md), read in [NOTE-770](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-770.md): Lemma 1.4, Theorem 3.2 and Theorem 3.4 with App. B. The operator g ↦ E[g(A)\|X] runs from L²(P_A) to L²(P_X) and is never assumed self-adjoint; its singular value decomposition comes from composing it with its adjoint. The guarantee is for linear probes and approximation error at the population level only. The thesis never works a non-reversible kernel on one space; the note of 2026-10-19 works a three-state one. It says nothing of what a trained network reaches. | Active |
| [THEORY-241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-241.md) | Same function, different internal decomposition | Kumar, Clune, Lehman & Stanley (2025), [LIT-944](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-944.md), read in [NOTE-771](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-771.md). For the skull, butterfly and apple CPPNs, SGD in the layerized evolved architecture fits the image, the network's whole function on the grid. It shows no reuse of the symmetric parts, and single-weight and random-direction sweeps distort the output, where the evolved networks' sweeps vary it meaningfully. Qualitative, curated and three images. The paper's account of why, the order of discovery in open-ended search, and its extension to large models are conjecture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-244](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-244.md) v3 | Shannon is expected Kolmogorov up to K(f) | Grünwald & Vitányi (2004), [LIT-224](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md), read in [NOTE-776](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-776.md). For computable f: 0 ≤ E_f K(x) − H(f) ≤ K(f) + O(1) (Thm 2.10), and I(X;Y) − K(f) < E I(x:y) < I(X;Y) + 2K(f) to O(1) (Thm 3.6), both re-derived by the record from domination of f by the universal distribution and the coding theorem; the entropy gap is attained by a point mass. The expected structure function is stated to bracket D*_m(R) and to equal D*(R) per symbol in the limit (Thm 6.27), but its right-hand step is asserted, so that bridge is not part of this account's claim ([QUESTION-208](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-208.md)). Sufficiency links only one way (Thm 5.13). None of this holds for a complex or unknown source, or for one string. | Active |
| [THEORY-246](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-246.md) v3 | Class separation hurts linear transfer | Kornblith, Chen, Lee & Norouzi (2021), [LIT-1044](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1044.md), read in [NOTE-762](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-762.md). Across nine objectives for ResNet-50 on ImageNet, penultimate class separation R² runs from 0.349 (softmax) to 0.845 (squared error), Papyan's Tr(Σ_W Σ_B†)/C from 21.2 to 0.33, and mean linear transfer to eight new-class datasets falls with R² (Spearman ρ = −0.93), from 75.9% to 48.3%. Cosine-softmax temperature raises R² from 0.24 to 0.77 and lowers transfer from 76.0% to 58.9%. CKA puts the differences in the last third of the network; fine-tuning erases them. The cost is for new classes: relearning the training classes, more separation helps. Networks early-stopped near 92% training accuracy; one dataset; correlational across losses. Promoted 2026-10-20 on this one study (ADR-047 v3), narrowed to what it measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-248](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-248.md) v3 | Rate-distortion bounds generalization error | Sefidgaran, Gohari, Richard & Şimşekli (COLT 2022), [LIT-236](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-236.md), read in [NOTE-780](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-780.md). Theorem 4: \|E gen\| ≤ √(2σ²·R_E(ε)/n) + ε, where R_E(ε) is the least I(S;Ŵ) over surrogates within ε in expected generalisation error. For a Lipschitz loss R_E is bounded by the rate-distortion function of P_W (Corollary 6). Theorem 10 is a tail version over a KL ball. The block-coding meaning is proved for finite alphabets only. No bound is evaluated for a learned model, and every bound depends on the unknown data distribution. | Active |
| [THEORY-253](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-253.md) v5 | Sign descent learns skills in sequence | Liu, Liu, Michaud, Gore and Tegmark (2025), [LIT-951](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-951.md), read in [NOTE-794](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-794.md). The Geometry model has loss Σ p_i L((θ − θ₀)·t_i) with orthogonal t_i. In it, SGD learns task 2 in time ∝ 1/p₂, while SignGD holds task 2 back until task 1 is done and then takes a constant extra delay (t₂/t₁ → 2). A rotated quadratic shows the split only when its eigendirections are misaligned with the coordinates (Fig. 12). The record reproduced both. The order is frequency order either way. The evidence is simulation and one fitted ODE; a derivation and a trained-network test are QUESTION-193. Sequential onset caused by dependency between skills is a separate experiment, not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-259](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-259.md) v3 | Ideal MDL and MAP agree when data are random | Vitányi & Li (1999/2000), [LIT-225](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-225.md), read in [NOTE-801](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-801.md). With the universal prior m and a recursive family Pr(·\|·), −log Pr(D\|H) − log m(H) = K(D\|H) + K(H) + d(D\|H) + O(1), where d(D\|H) = log(m(D\|H)/Pr(D\|H)) is the universal randomness deficiency of D for H; d ≥ −K(Pr(·\|·)) − O(1), and d is bounded exactly when D is Martin-Löf random for H. So ideal MDL and MAP agree to within a constant on admissible hypotheses (Theorems 3–5, re-derived by the record) and part where the data are not random for the hypothesis (0ⁿ against the fair coin). The paper's slack α = K(Pr(·\|H)) + K(P) is an upper bound, not the gap. | Active |
| [THEORY-263](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-263.md) v3 | Variable-rate bounds give PAC-Bayes | Sefidgaran & Zaidi (2023; IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 2024), [LIT-233](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-233.md), read in [NOTE-806](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-806.md). Theorem 1: with a sample-dependent rate R_{S,W}, gen ≤ √(4σ²(R_{S,W} + log(√(2n)/δ))/(2n−1) + ε). With R_{S,W} = log dP_{W\|S}/dP(W) the coding condition holds at ε = 0 and the bound is the disintegrated PAC-Bayes bound. The general Theorems 3–5 recover Rivasplata et al.'s PAC-Bayes bound and Xu–Raginsky's. The coding construction is proved for finite alphabets only. The general proofs are change of measure. The rate is a Shannon code-length difference against a prior, not Kolmogorov complexity. | Active |
| [THEORY-266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-266.md) v3 | Trajectory rate-distortion bounds generalization | Sefidgaran & Zaidi (2023), [LIT-233](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-233.md), Theorem 7, read in [NOTE-806](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-806.md). For an L-Lipschitz loss in [0, 1], with probability ≥ 1 − δ, the mean of gen(S, W^t) over iterations is at most √((RD(S, ε; π_S) + log(√(2n)M/δ))/(2n − 1) + 4Lε). RD is computed for the sample at hand. The coupling coefficient M depends on the unknown distribution and absorbs I(W^T; S). The CIFAR-10 experiment drops M and 4Lε and shows only that the estimated rate and the test gap fall together over learning rates. For FCN4 the plotted rate term is about 3, which is vacuous for 0–1 loss. | Active |
| [THEORY-270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-270.md) v4 | Shared nonsense enables unsupervised translation | Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise (NeurIPS 2023), [LIT-941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-941.md), read in [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md). Proved for maximum likelihood in stylised random models with uniform languages and one-to-one translators; in one model the bound O(log\|Θ\| / (α·min(m,\|T\|))) is tight up to a constant. Information- theoretic only. The prior substitutes for parallel data in learning the decoder, not for information in a message. | Active |
| [THEORY-274](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-274.md) | Sequence models store graphs as geometry | Noroozizadeh, Nagarajan, Rosenfeld & Kumar (2025), [LIT-995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-995.md), read in [NOTE-800](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-800.md). Empirical throughout: path-star graphs up to 5×10⁴ nodes, four tiny graphs, frozen-embedding controls; the two-layer spectral analysis is informal and rests on an unproved observation (App. F). It does not explain why deeper models prefer the geometry, which the paper poses as open, and its main transformer runs used weight decay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-277.md) v2 | Shortest two-part code gives best-fit model | Vereshchagin & Vitányi (2002/2004), [LIT-239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-239.md), read in [NOTE-787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-787.md), Theorem IV.8: β_x(α) + K(x) and λ_x(α) agree to within O(log n) for a string of length n. Every set minimising K(S) + log \|S\| at complexity α is within O(log n) of the best fit there. h_x and λ_x are upper semicomputable, while β_x is not semicomputable. Restated by Grünwald & Vitányi, [LIT-224](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md), §6.2. Finite-set models; computable distributions at O(log n) cost. It says nothing at the (k/2) log n scale of parametric model selection, and nothing about K(A) + K(x \| A). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md) v5 | MSE training follows a central path to collapse | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). MSE loss splits exactly into a least-squares term and a non-negative deviation term, and the deviation becomes negligible early in training in 15 dataset–network cells. On that central path, with λ = 0, the loss is ½ Σ 1/(ω_j² + C) in the singular values of Σ_W^(−1/2)M̃. Under a flow that re-whitens the features after every step, each ω_j grows as (4t/N)^(1/4), and their ratios tend to 1. That is NC1 and NC2, and NC3–NC4 follow. Not shown: that ordinary training is this flow, or anything for cross-entropy or with weight decay. | Active |
| [THEORY-279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-279.md) v2 | Networks learn low-order statistics first | Belrose et al. (2024, ICML), [LIT-952](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-952.md), read in [NOTE-777](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-777.md). Over training, ConvNeXt V2, Swin V2 and RegNet-Y on five small image datasets are probed with images whose class means or covariances are grafted from another class, and with maximum-entropy samples that keep only those statistics. Accuracy on these rises and then falls, often below chance. Pythia fits unigram-sampled text before bigram-sampled text. The ordering is empirical and covers orders one and two. The Taylor argument that motivates it is a heuristic, and the paper does not measure an ordered sequence beyond second order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-283](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-283.md) v3 | Hierarchical features emerge one at a time | Defilippis, Krzakala, Loureiro and Maillard (2026), [LIT-940](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-940.md), read in [NOTE-805](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-805.md). Take x ~ N(0, I/d), n = αd, and f⋆ = Σ a_k g_k(⟨w_k, x⟩) with even links of generative exponent two and a_k ~ k^(−γ). Direction k is weakly recoverable at α_k = Θ(a_k^(−2)) (Thm. 3.2). The optimal weighted error is Θ(α^(−1+1/(2γ))) until α ≍ m⋆^(2γ). The spectral estimator on Σ T(y_i)x_ix_iᵀ attains both (Thm. 3.6). The cascade is in the number of samples, not in training time. The network result is for a spectral first layer plus a ridge readout, not gradient descent. | Active |
| [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md) v2 | Imbalance yields SELI, not simplex ETF | Thrampoulidis et al. (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md). For the unconstrained-features max-margin problem under STEP imbalance, every solution has logits ŴᵀĤ = Ẑ (one-hot minus 1/k), ĤᵀĤ = UΛUᵀ and ŴᵀŴ = VΛVᵀ from Ẑ's SVD (Theorem 1). This is the ETF only if the data are balanced or binary. No finite ridge gives it under imbalance (Proposition 1), though the ridge path tends to it (Proposition 2). ResNet-18 and VGG-13 runs sit closer to SELI than to the ETF, and approach it more slowly at larger R. Not shown: that gradient descent reaches it, and anything with more than one seed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-289](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-289.md) v3 | Keeping data bounds model-collapse error | Gerstgrasser, Schaeffer, Dey et al. (2024), [LIT-971](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-971.md), read in [NOTE-815](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-815.md), Theorems 1–2 extending Dohmatob et al.'s replace result. Proved for ridgeless OLS with isotropic Gaussian features, the real covariates reused every round and only labels regenerated. The error is bounded, not constant: it rises every round towards its limit, and every model remains a noisier copy of the first. Small language and diffusion models behave alike over five to eight rounds; a VAE's error still rises. | Active |
| [THEORY-293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-293.md) v4 | Facts are learned past a capacity threshold | Gu, Lyu, Li and Zhang (2025), [LIT-984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-984.md), read in [NOTE-796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-796.md). Proved for an idealised learner whose capacity is mutual information with the data (Theorem 4.3), on an orthogonal mixture of uniform facts and a second domain; seen in Pythia models from 14M to 6.9B on synthetic biographies mixed into web text. The theory is static. It does not say when in training the facts arrive, and it does not show that SGD reaches the optimal allocation. | Active |
| [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) v4 | Lazy training leaves NC1 where it started | Kothapalli & Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md). NC1 = tr Σ_W / tr Σ_B of kernel-defined features is a ratio of linear functionals of the kernel matrix (Theorem 4.1). For one-dimensional data, two classes on opposite sides of the origin and zero bias, the ReLU tangent kernel of a wide two-layer net is a constant multiple of the NNGP kernel, so NC1 is the same (Theorem 5.1, re-derived). In higher dimensions it is measured no lower, and for ReLU higher; whether lazy training leaves NC1 in place there is [QUESTION-192](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-192.md). The inference that collapse requires feature learning is the reading's, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-314](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-314.md) v2 | RKHS minimizers lie in the training kernels' span | Schölkopf, Herbrich & Smola (2001), [LIT-261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-261.md), Theorem 1 with its proof (eqs. 18–24), read in [NOTE-836](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-836.md) and checked. No convexity of the cost and no Riesz theorem is used; the RKHS is built from the kernel, so the reproducing property holds by construction. The theorem is stated over countable kernel expansions of finite norm, assumes a minimizer exists, and does not cover costs that see f other than through its values at the training points. | Active |
| [THEORY-318](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-318.md) v3 | DP bounds max-information, hence overfitting | Dwork, Feldman, Hardt, Pitassi, Reingold & Roth (2015), [LIT-964](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-964.md), Supplementary Material only, read in [NOTE-848](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-848.md) (Skimmed: the main text was not reached). Theorem 2 and Lemma 5 are proved there and were checked: P[overfit] ≤ 2^{I∞}·max P[overfit], and ε-DP gives I∞ ≤ log₂e·εn. Thresholdout's guarantee (Theorem 11), n = O(ln(m/β)/τ²·min{B, √(B ln(m/β))/τ}), is stated with its proof elsewhere. Statistical queries on a discrete universe only, and a procedure that prevents inflation, not a correction for a search already run. | Active |
| [THEORY-319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-319.md) v3 | Contrastive ratio's linear readout nears Bayes | Tosh, Krishnamurthy & Hsu (2021), [LIT-251](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-251.md), read in [NOTE-841](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-841.md): Lemma 1, §2.3–2.4, Lemma 2 and Theorem 3. The label enters only through how redundant the views are about it; the representation is the density ratio p(x,z)/(p(x)p(z)), learned without labels. Population level. The error-propagation results need a uniform bound on the ratio, and the low-dimensional direct embeddings are shown to exist, not to be reached. | Active |
| [THEORY-320](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-320.md) v2 | Known classes steer which novel classes are found | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). On the population graph, at the exact rank-k optimum, R(U*, y) = ‖(I − P_{L♭})U♭ᵀy‖² (Theorem 5.5, stated as ≤, proved as = in C.1). In a one-sample-per-kind toy, a known class sharing colour makes a colour labelling recoverable, and one sharing shape makes it worse than none (Lemma 5.4). The general error bound (Theorem 5.6) is approximate and pools all known classes into one block, and is not part of this account. Nothing here is about trained networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-331](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-331.md) | High inference volume shifts compute up front | Sardana et al. (2024; arXiv 2023), [LIT-1070](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1070.md), read in [NOTE-881](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-881.md), and Snell et al. (2024), [LIT-1063](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1063.md), read in [NOTE-869](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-869.md). Sardana et al. minimise training plus lifetime inference FLOPs at a fixed loss under a Chinchilla-fitted law: the optimum moves to smaller models trained longer as known demand grows (28% fewer FLOPs at 30B quality and 10^13 inference tokens), and 47 runs show loss still falling at extreme ratios but more slowly than the law predicts. Snell et al. match FLOPs between a small model with test-time search or revision and a ~14× larger model on MATH: test-time compute wins at a low ratio of inference to pretraining tokens on easier questions and loses at a high ratio, and on the hardest at every ratio. Both take expected use as a known aggregate; neither has staleness or uncertainty about demand, and Snell's evidence is one model family on 500 questions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-342](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-342.md) v3 | Training and search compute trade log-linearly | Jones (2021), [LIT-1069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1069.md), read in [NOTE-884](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-884.md). Across about 200 AlphaZero models on Hex boards 3×3 to 9×9, the best Elo for a given training compute follows one change-point curve, shifted by a fixed factor of compute per board row. On 9×9 only, iso-Elo contours of training against test-time search compute are straight in log–log space (fit: log test = −1.2·log train + 0.004·Elo + 29) over roughly 1e14–1e16 FLOPS-seconds of training, ending at a one-node search. One game, one nonstandard implementation, no uncertainty on the fitted coefficients, and no count of how many searches the trained agent will run, so it gives an exchange rate, not an amortization. | Active |
| [THEORY-349](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-349.md) | OI to bounded tests is multicalibration | Dwork, Kim, Reingold, Rothblum and Yona (2021), [LIT-1068](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1068.md), read in [NOTE-885](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-885.md), and Hébert-Johnson, Kim, Reingold and Rothblum (2018), [LIT-1052](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1052.md), read in [NOTE-879](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-879.md). A predictor is outcome indistinguishable relative to a class of distinguishers when none can tell nature's outcomes from outcomes drawn from the predictor, up to ε. With no access or sample access to the predictor this is equivalent to multi-accuracy or multicalibration over closely related classes, and a predictor meeting it exists at size O(s/ε²) (O(s/α⁴γ) for multicalibration), independent of nature. Learning a multicalibrated predictor is equivalent to weak agnostic learning of the class. Adequacy here is relative to the class, the outcome and the features, and is not unique; it is not closeness to the truth, and the papers say nothing about signal detection. | Active |
| [THEORY-354](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-354.md) v2 | Refutation power depends on access to predictor | Dwork, Kim, Reingold, Rothblum and Yona (2021), [LIT-1068](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1068.md), read in [NOTE-885](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-885.md). Against sample-access distinguishers of size s an outcome-indistinguishable predictor of size O(s/ε²) always exists. Against oracle-access distinguishers, under fine-grained hardness of clique counting or BPP ≠ PSPACE, there are natures and polynomially many cheap distinguishers such that no predictor much cheaper than nature is indistinguishable. Non-adaptive queries add little; the power comes from adaptive queries. The results are conditional and asymptotic, with upper and lower bounds in different parameterisations; they say nothing about human observers or about which access a real auditor has. | Active |
| [THEORY-359](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-359.md) | Resource-rational analysis rederives heuristics | Lieder & Griffiths (2020; online 2019), [LIT-1071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1071.md), read in [NOTE-873](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-873.md). Resource rationality picks the heuristic that maximizes expected utility of its result minus the expected opportunity cost of the time and resources it uses (Eq. 3), averaged over environments consistent with what is known (Eq. 4), and a five-step method derives process models from it. The support is a review of others' models recast in this frame, with numbers from those studies. The authors offer optimality as a methodological device, not a claim about people, and the method lets constraints be refitted to data. The objective is per episode, with no terms for storing, retrieving or reusing a result, or for its going stale. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-439](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-439.md) v4 | Test-time training beats in-context alone | Akyürek et al. (2024; ICML 2025), [LIT-796](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-796.md), read in [NOTE-637](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-637.md). On BIG-Bench Hard with Llama 3.1 8B and 10 demonstrations over five seeds, zero-shot 40.9%, in-context 50.5%, per-task LoRA test-time training then in-context 57.8%; 12 of 27 tasks gain at least 2 points, and Boolean expressions falls. Training the update on leave-one-out in-context tasks beats training on bare pairs (57.8% against 51.5%). The update is discarded after each task, so it is as transient as a context. It is two benchmarks and one model family, and which task property predicts the gain is open. | Active |
| [THEORY-481](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-481.md) v4 | Linear attention learns staged by input spectrum | Mainali & Teixeira (2025), [LIT-859](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-859.md), read in [NOTE-658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-658.md). The prediction of one linear-attention layer reduces to p₂ W Σ̂_x q₁ x_q, a product of two learned factors, so averaged gradient flow decouples into modes with τ_α dp_α/dt = q_α(1 − p_α q_α s^∞_α) and τ_α = (ηP s_α²)⁻¹, logistic from a balanced start. The fixed point is ŷ = W Σ̂_x Σ_x⁻¹ x_q as N → ∞. The paper's finite-N form, the one Ahn et al. and Zhang, Frei & Bartlett found, holds at finite N only for isotropic inputs with equal modes. The trajectory is new. The decoupling into independent modes is exact as N → ∞. At finite N it holds only for isotropic inputs with equal modes: the paper commutes the non-diagonal empirical covariance at (A71) and (A73), and the correct Wishart moment couples the modes at order 1/N. Alignment of the weights with the data's eigenbasis is assumed throughout, the null blocks vanish only in expectation over tasks, and the transfer to non-linear transformers is timing coincidences. | Active |
| [THEORY-510](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-510.md) | Crop tolerance varies by class; some classes lose | Balestriero, Bottou & LeCun (2022), [LIT-234](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-234.md), read in [NOTE-845](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-845.md). Six pretrained models on cropped test images keep some classes recognisable at an 8% crop and lose others below about 50%, and agree on which. Over 20 ResNet-50 runs, moving the crop lower bound from 100% to 8% raises mean accuracy from about 70% to 76% while "academic gown" falls from about 62% to 40%. The classes shown are hand-picked; the per-class test rejects for 4.4% of classes at the 5% level, uncorrected for 1,000 tests, which alone is not more than chance; and evaluation-set noise is not counted. Theorem 1 does not reach which classes pay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-521.md) | Generalization error can jump at critical load | Martin & Mahoney (2017), [LIT-672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-672.md), read in [NOTE-542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-542.md), restating Seung, Sompolinsky & Tishby (1992) and Haussler, Kearns, Seung & Tishby (1996), which the record does not hold. Generalization is set by maximizing s(ε) − α ln(1/(1 − ε)). For weights on a sphere s(ε) ~ ln ε and ε ~ 1/α; for ±1 weights s(ε) ~ −(π²/2)ε² ln ε, the first-order condition has no solution past a critical load, and the error drops to zero. Uniform bounds that see a class only through its size or VC dimension are smooth and blind to this. That deep networks have such a phase diagram is the authors' conjecture, and their mapping of label noise to load and early stopping to temperature is an analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-574](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-574.md) | Width bound is metric, and doesn't entail routing | Li (2026), [LIT-376](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md) (Local Urysohn Width, v1), [LIT-375](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md) (Structural Learning Theory) and [LIT-374](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) (Structural Decoupling), read jointly in [NOTE-323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-323.md), [NOTE-324](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-324.md) and [NOTE-322](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-322.md). In repaired form the formal core holds: width is incomparable with the per-cell VC dimension, fewer cells than width give an error floor (under an assumption that states it), and discovering all basins costs Ω(w log w) samples. But local correctness is automatic on any connected patch, the bouquet lower bound is metric (the paper's Remark 8.11 concedes it), a global classifier has width 1 (Remark 3.4), and the additive Rademacher bound said to call for decoupled training holds for joint training too. | Active |
| [THEORY-614](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-614.md) v3 | ICL can be Bayesian inference over concepts | Xie, Raghunathan, Liang & Ma (2021), [LIT-797](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-797.md), read in [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md). Theorem 1 is proved under Assumptions 1–5 and a distinguishability condition; Theorems 2–3 give roughly 1/k excess risk without it. The proofs were not followed in the reading. [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md) declined a THEORY because the result is conditional on exact fit to a specific generative model, so it is a consequence of that model, not a fact about language models. It is filed Proposed under the owner's ruling, with the condition in the title. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) | Weight decay on factors is nuclear-norm penalty | Boncoraglio et al. (2025), [LIT-857](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-857.md), Appendix A, read in [NOTE-661](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-661.md), and re-derived here. ‖W‖²_F = Tr(WWᵀ) = ‖WWᵀ‖_*, since a PSD matrix's singular values are its eigenvalues. For untied factors, Hölder's inequality for Schatten norms and AM–GM bound ‖M‖_* by (‖U‖²_F + ‖V‖²_F)/2 over every factorization UVᵀ = M, and the balanced SVD factorization attains it. The product's rank is bounded by the factors' inner dimension. It says nothing about what the trained product looks like, which is [THEORY-180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-180.md)'s spectral law. | Active |
| [THEORY-735](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-735.md) | Batch size trades steps against examples | McCandlish, Kaplan, Amodei et al. (2018), [LIT-348](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-348.md), §2 and App. D.1, as read and re-derived in [NOTE-293](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-293.md). A derivation under stated assumptions: a second-order model of the loss along the step, an unbiased minibatch gradient of covariance Σ/B, and the step size that maximises the expected decrease. It says nothing about whether real training meets those assumptions, or how well the noise scale predicts the measured critical batch, which is [THEORY-033](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-033.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-737](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-737.md) | Novel labels' residual is what known rows miss | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), Theorem 5.5 with its proof in C.1, read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). The paper states the identity as ≤, and its proof is a chain of equalities. Re-derived here in three steps from orthogonality and least squares. With the paper's Lemma 5.1 it bounds the novel labelling's 0–1 linear-probe error by twice this residual. It is about the exact rank-k factorization of a population graph, not about trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-738](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-738.md) v2 | Imbalanced max-margin optimum is simplex labels | Thrampoulidis, Kini, Vakilian and Behnia (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), Theorem 1 and Corollary 1.3, read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md) and re-derived here. By [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) the problem is nuclear-norm minimisation of the logits under margin constraints. The polar factor of the simplex-encoded label matrix certifies it optimal, because under step imbalance its off-diagonal entries are negative. It does not say that gradient descent or trained networks reach this geometry, which is [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-739](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-739.md) v2 | word2vec proxy learns eigenvectors in sequence | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md), Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, read in [NOTE-660](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-660.md) and re-derived here. The quartic proxy is a function of WWᵀ alone, so von Neumann's trace inequality gives its rank-d minimisers. Gradient flow from an aligned start keeps the eigenbasis and reduces each mode to a logistic equation. It does not say that word2vec, or the proxy from random initialisation, behaves this way; that is [THEORY-182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-740](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-740.md) v2 | Deep linear nets learn modes one at a time | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014, 2019), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md) and [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md) and [NOTE-666](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-666.md), re-derived here. From a decoupled, balanced start the two-layer equations keep the SVD basis of Σyx, and each mode's strength obeys τȧ = 2a(s − a), a logistic rise. One weight matrix on the same data relaxes every mode exponentially on the one timescale τ. It does not say that random starts follow the solution, which is [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-759](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-759.md) | Network fits low frequencies first regardless | Rahaman et al. (2019), [LIT-1261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1261.md), Experiment 1, read in full in [NOTE-983](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-983.md). With equal amplitudes, and with amplitudes rising from 0.1 at 5 cycles to 1 at 50, the normalised fit \|f̃(k_i)\|/A_i reaches 1 at low frequency first. This is the reverse of the order by strength that [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) gives for a deep linear network. One architecture, one optimiser, a 1-D input, ten runs averaged. The paper's theory gives a bound on speed, not this order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-761](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-761.md) v2 | Piecewise-linear Fourier decay is k^(−d−1) | Rahaman et al. (2019), [LIT-1261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1261.md), read in full in [NOTE-983](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-983.md). One integration by parts turns f̃ into a sum of polytope transforms weighted by the region gradients and divided by k. Each further step of Diaz et al.'s recursion gains another 1/k until the path reaches a face whose directions are all orthogonal to k. Generic directions reach the vertices, giving k^(−d−1), and every direction gets at least k^(−2). It is a bound on what a piecewise-linear function contains, not a statement about training. Unbounded ReLU networks fall outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-778](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-778.md) v2 | Level-ℓ correlations need P ≈ v m^(2ℓ−1) samples | Cagnetta and Wyart (2024), [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md), App. D–F, read in [NOTE-687](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-687.md); re-derived to leading order by the promotion audit and checked against exact covariances of sampled grammars. A statement about the statistics of the generative model only: it says nothing about what a trained network learns, or when, and nothing about natural language. | Active |
| [THEORY-779](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-779.md) v2 | Momentum SGD's stationary spread follows Hessian | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), §§4–6 and App. G, read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md); the stationary moments re-derived by the promotion audit. An exact result for a model: Σ ∝ H constant and a quadratic loss are assumptions, and nothing here says a deep network meets them. The probability current is nonzero but reversible: under the model's assumptions the stationary process is time-reversible once velocities are flipped, so it is "broken detailed balance" only in the paper's sense, a nonzero current. | Active |
| [THEORY-781](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-781.md) | Strong SGD noise makes symmetric subspaces attract | Ziyin (2024), [LIT-1014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1014.md), read in [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md). Beyond the exact half that [THEORY-213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-213.md) holds, the paper argues by a Lyapunov-exponent analysis that strong SGD noise makes a mirror's subspace attracting even at a strict saddle, and reads sparsity, low rank and identical neurons in trained networks as its result. That analysis rests on a second-order, diagonal- Hessian approximation, and the network evidence is a ResNet18's correlation blocks. The test is [QUESTION-206](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-206.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-782](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-782.md) | Grokking onset: pairs fix the representation | Liu, Kitouni, Nolte, Michaud, Tegmark and Williams (2022), [LIT-858](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md), read in [NOTE-662](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-662.md), with Power et al.'s critical fraction ([LIT-341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-341.md)). The paper presents the critical training fraction as where the training set's equations fix the embedding. [THEORY-181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md) holds the theorem for the ideal model and the match at the one size measured, p = 10 with 1D embeddings. Held to addition: for S₃ the networks generalise beyond this mechanism. The multi-size test is [QUESTION-199](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-199.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-783](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-783.md) v2 | Adam makes skills compete and emerge in sequence | Liu, Liu, Michaud, Gore and Tegmark (2025), [LIT-951](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-951.md), read in [NOTE-794](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-794.md). The paper explains the Domino effect, skills starting as others finish, by a coordinate-wise optimizer's competition for update signs. [THEORY-253](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-253.md) holds the simulation in their Geometry model and the rotated quadratic. The paper also shows dependent skills starting after their prerequisites (C5), so the optimizer is one source of sequential onset, not the only one. The test in a trained network is [QUESTION-193](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-193.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-784](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-784.md) | Data-limited loss falls as context horizon grows | Cagnetta, Raventós, Ganguli and Wyart (2026), [LIT-888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-888.md), read in [NOTE-689](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-689.md), building on Cagnetta and Wyart's effective context window ([LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md)). The paper presents the horizon as the reason the data-limited exponent is γ/(2β). [THEORY-204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-204.md) holds what it showed: the derivation under assumed scaling forms, and the measured overlap on TinyStories and WikiText-103 up to about 10^8 tokens. Whether the horizon is why is the test [QUESTION-233](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-233.md) asks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-786](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-786.md) | Nets learn grammar when correlations beat noise | Cagnetta, Petrini, Tomasini, Favero and Wyart (2023), [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md), propose that deep networks learn compositional data by detecting the correlations between input patches and the class, and that the sample complexity is where those correlations emerge from sampling noise. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md), the measured law and the synonym-invariance it coincides with. This is the mechanism, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-788](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-788.md) | Training past zero error yields neural collapse | Papyan, Han and Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), title their paper on the "prevalence" of neural collapse and present it as a pervasive outcome of the terminal phase of training. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), only what their runs measured: three architectures with cross-entropy on seven balanced datasets without augmentation. This is the general law, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-790](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-790.md) | SGD noise balances rescaling-symmetric groups | Ziyin, Li & Ueda, [LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md), with the Itô term from [LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md). The law of balance is proved in the SDE model of SGD, and that part is the Active [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md). The authors present the law as general to networks with rescaling symmetry, but test it only on small synthetic networks. This THEORY holds the general claim, for deep networks on real data, which no measurement in the record yet supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-792](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-792.md) | Orthogonal init keeps deep linear training fast | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md). The exact depth law is proved only from decoupled, balanced starts, and that part is the Active [THEORY-187](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-187.md). Beyond it, the paper argues from MNIST runs and random-matrix simulations that random orthogonal layers are such a start in effect, because their product is an isometry, while scaled Gaussian layers are not. This THEORY holds that wider claim, which is argued and simulated and not derived. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-793](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-793.md) | Barlow Twins learns eigenvectors one at a time | Simon et al. (2023), [LIT-242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md), read in [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md). The stepwise dynamics, the minimum-norm end point and the kernel-PCA form are proved from aligned initialization, and that part is the Active [THEORY-229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md). Generic small initialization rests on the paper's Result 4.6, which its authors style a result and derive informally in App. C, with numerical checks at d = 3. This THEORY holds that generic case. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-794](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-794.md) | Compositional generalization needs diverse combos | Uselis, Dittadi & Oh (2025), [LIT-667](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-667.md), read in [NOTE-525](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-525.md). Their title and abstract present diversity of combinations, not data volume, as what drives compositional generalization in vision models. Their evidence is ResNet-50s trained from scratch on two-concept grids, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, and that measured part, with the factorization theorem, is the Active [THEORY-117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md). This THEORY holds the general causal claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-797](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-797.md) v2 | MSE nets reach collapse along the central path | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021; ICLR 2022), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). The paper's proposed explanation of neural collapse under MSE in real networks, filed apart from its measured central-path proximity and its derivation in a renormalized model ([THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. Renormalization is imposed, not measured, and every experiment used weight decay, which the derivation excludes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-806](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-806.md) | Translation without parallel data is learnable | The general reading that [THEORY-270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-270.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the common-nonsense model its bound is proved in (batch 044). Goldwasser, Gruber, Kalai and Paradise (NeurIPS 2023), [LIT-941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-941.md), read in [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md), motivate their framework by translating animal communication and state its lesson for translation in general, while saying their stylised models are not intended to capture natural language. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-809](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-809.md) | LMs learn facts at the capacity-optimal point | The link that [THEORY-293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-293.md)'s title asserted before the promotion audit narrowed it (batch 036) to the optimal learner's theorem and the observation of a threshold in Pythia models. Gu, Lyu, Li and Zhang (2025), [LIT-984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-984.md), read in [NOTE-796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-796.md), explain the trained models' thresholds by the optimal learner's. The one quantitative check, a size exponent of 1.152 against a predicted 1.283, is recorded against it. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-813](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-813.md) v2 | Lazy training doesn't produce neural collapse | The general reading that [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one-dimensional, zero-bias, two-class case it proves. Kothapalli and Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md), draw it as their conclusion: the lazy regime does not collapse anything, so the data-dependence of collapse has to come from a kernel that moves with the data. Beyond the solved case their support is simulation on two-class Gaussian data, where the NTK comes out less collapsed than the NNGP. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-839](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-839.md) | Stable points lie within 2L_zε/γ of the optimum | Perdomo, Zrnic, Mendler-Dünner and Hardt (2020), [LIT-1336](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1336.md), read in [NOTE-1044](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1044.md). Self-consistency under one's own influence and the best outcome under that influence are different targets. The bound says they are close when the influence is weak relative to the loss's curvature. It does not say how to find the optimum, which needs the distribution map away from the deployed model. | Active |
| [THEORY-840](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-840.md) | V-information is estimable in high dimension | Xu, Zhao, Song, Stewart and Ermon (2020), [LIT-1309](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1309.md), read in [NOTE-1048](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1048.md), Theorem 1. Restricting the predictor class trades the data-processing inequality for estimability. The bound needs bounded log-likelihoods and says nothing about Shannon information, which a restricted family may under- or over-state ([THEORY-846](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-846.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-846](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-846.md) v3 | Computation can create V-information | Xu, Zhao, Song, Stewart and Ermon (2020), [LIT-1309](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1309.md), read in [NOTE-1048](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1048.md), define V-information and say it "can be created through computation". The record's worked case is [CLAIM-199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md)'s XOR under the paper's linear families, and its addition is the ceiling: usable information never exceeds the source's Shannon information when V can predict the marginal of Y without input, and can exceed it when V cannot. It says nothing about which family a real observer has. | Active |
| [THEORY-861](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-861.md) v2 | Repeated retraining converges if ε < γ/β | Perdomo, Zrnic, Mendler-Dünner and Hardt (2020), [LIT-1336](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1336.md), read in [NOTE-1044](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1044.md). Retraining under performativity is a fixed-point iteration, and these are the conditions for it to settle. Its fixed point is self-consistent, not optimal ([THEORY-839](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-839.md)), and outside the conditions there may be several or none. | Active |
| [THEORY-899](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-899.md) v2 | Imitating populations run replicator learning | Soma et al.'s Propositions 1 and 2, read in full from arXiv v6 in [NOTE-1132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1132.md), with both proofs and the aggregation in Eqs. 8–14 re-derived. An exact identity of expected updates under idealizing assumptions: infinite N, large well-mixed neighbourhoods, and imitation decoupled from evaluation. Each member is one parallel action sample, α = 1/N plays the learning rate, and the macro-policy is a stateless bandit policy over the members' types. | Active |
| [THEORY-905](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-905.md) | Finite imitation populations lock on a suboptimum | Soma et al.'s simulations and limits section, read in [NOTE-1132](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1132.md). With ten options and arbitrary parameters that the authors call qualitative, swarms of about 500 track the replicator dynamic and smaller ones often lock onto worse options. The authors state that pure imitation can delete a type and has no mechanism for escape in non-stationary environments. Hybrids that compare qualities are faster. Simulation-scoped, not a theorem. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-925](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-925.md) v3 | Counterfactual baseline credits each agent | Foerster et al.'s counterfactual baseline (COMA, Eq. 4 and Appendix A of arXiv v3), read in full in [NOTE-1152](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1152.md), with the zero-expectation step re-derived. A proved property of the estimator, not of performance. Its counterfactual is "had the agent acted as it usually does", not "had it not acted", and its values are a learned critic's, trained on occasions when each alternative was taken; it presupposes those occasions. | Active |
| [THEORY-927](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-927.md) v3 | MoE gates collapse without balancing loss | Shazeer et al. (2017), section 4 and Appendix A, read in full in [NOTE-1145](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1145.md) from arXiv v1. The imbalance is reported in one paragraph, with Table 6's no-loss row as its evidence: one architecture, ten epochs, no variance. The mechanism is the authors' explanation, not a tested result. The fix penalizes unequal use regardless of competence. | Active |
| [THEORY-928](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-928.md) v3 | Memory decay makes softmax learning dissipative | Sato & Crutchfield (arXiv 2002; PRE 2003), [LIT-1520](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1520.md), read in full from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1144](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1144.md), Eqs. 1–13. The entropy-like term is what memory decay becomes under softmax choice. The limit, the dissipation rate and the Hamiltonian were re-derived, second-checked at the status review of 2026-10-30. The model updates every action's memory at the same rate, so it is the full-information case, not Q-learning as usually run. | Active |
| [THEORY-929](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-929.md) v3 | Monotonic mixing allows decentralised greedy | Rashid et al.'s QMIX (ICML 2018), read in full in [NOTE-1154](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1154.md), with QTRAN ([NOTE-1141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1141.md)) for the strictness. Monotonicity is sufficient for the greedy-profile property and not necessary. It presupposes a real- valued joint value: what it adds is that each member's ranking of its own actions agrees with the collective's whatever the others do, an ordinal separability condition. It is Wolpert and Tumer's factoredness stated for values. | Active |
| [THEORY-930](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-930.md) v2 | Nash clusters widest at intermediate strength | Czarnecki et al. (2020), [LIT-1504](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1504.md), section 6 and supplements E–I, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1146.md). Agents were MinMax at depths 0–9, loss-seeking MaxMin and MCTS, with 50 seeds each, about 1000 distinct per game after duplicates were removed. Games: Hex, Go and Quoridor on small boards, Tic-Tac-Toe, its misère form and Connect Four. AlphaStar's league shows its training system's geometry, the authors say. A qualitative profile with a fitted skew-normal curve and no test. | Active |
| [THEORY-931](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-931.md) | Opponent shaping reaches tit-for-tat | Foerster et al.'s LOLA (AAMAS 2018), read in full in [NOTE-1150](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1150.md) from arXiv v4, with the update rule re-derived. Empirical, in two small games and a grid game. Shaping here is mutual and produced cooperation, not capture; in matching pennies, a harmonic game, it damped the cycling of naive learners. Table 3's naive-learner tit-for-tat figure (20.8%) does not square with their return (−1.98), and the NOTE says so. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-932](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-932.md) v3 | Frequency-adjusted Q-learning follows replicator | Kaisers & Tuyls (AAMAS 2010), [LIT-1511](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1511.md), read in full in [NOTE-1140](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1140.md), correcting the model of Tuyls, Verbeeck & Lenaerts (2003), [LIT-1501](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1501.md), which is not read. The derivation of the discrepancy and of the frequency adjustment was re-derived and second-checked at the status review of 2026-10-30. The experiments are three games, one temperature, compared by eye; whether Q-learning departs in general is [THEORY-1234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1234.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-933](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-933.md) v3 | IGM is strictly weaker than monotonic factoring | Son et al.'s QTRAN (ICML 2019), read in full in [NOTE-1141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1141.md), with Theorem 1 and the single-state observation re-derived. IGM presupposes a real-valued joint value and constrains only the optimum: members may rank everything below it differently from the collective. With full observability it is nearly empty; its content is whether members acting on local histories can each pick their part of the optimum. | Active |
| [THEORY-936](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-936.md) | Softmax RPS learners show Hamiltonian chaos | Sato & Crutchfield (arXiv 2002; PRE 2003), [LIT-1520](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1520.md), read in full in [NOTE-1144](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1144.md), pp. 2–3 and Figs. 1–3. Numerical results for one game, two agents and the parameters shown; the zero-decay, zero-sum case was first reported in Sato, Akiyama and Farmer (PNAS 2002), which is not held. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-937](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-937.md) v2 | Mixture of experts learns faster and specializes | Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan and Hinton (1991), read in full in [NOTE-1147](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1147.md) from a scan of the published article. The gradients of Eqs. 1.4 and 1.5 were re-derived when filed. The task is small (two formants, 75 speakers, 25 runs per system) and has two natural subtasks; the idle experts are read by the authors as economy, and their recovery is not tested. | Active |
| [THEORY-941](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-941.md) | Regret matching reaches correlated equilibria | Hart & Mas-Colell (Econometrica 2000; handout 1996), [LIT-1521](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1521.md), read in full in [NOTE-1142](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1142.md). Convergence is of time-averaged joint frequencies to a set, not of play to an equilibrium; the common history is the correlating device; inertia is needed; and interior correlated equilibria that are not pure Nash cannot be the limit. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-945](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-945.md) v2 | Mean field Q reduces many agents to two bodies | Yang et al. (2018), read in full in [NOTE-1148](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1148.md) from arXiv v5. The expansion and the remainder bound were re-derived when filed and second-checked on 2026-10-30; the appendix states an equality where only an inequality holds, which leaves the bound intact. The convergence theorem is reported, not held.
