Its contraction step needs a high temperature while it assumes a greedy limit, and the cancellation of remainders is argued from homogeneity, not proved. The approximation requires agents interchangeable within a neighbourhood. Whether the method works as claimed is [THEORY-1231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1231.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-947](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-947.md) | Partial-monitoring approachability at T^-1/3 | Kwon and Perchet (2017), [LIT-1526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1526.md), read in [NOTE-1159](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1159.md). The rates are for the average payoff's distance to the target, uniformly over Nature's choices, with approachability assumed (Perchet's condition). Optimal means not improvable in the worst case over games. It gives no guarantee for individual stages or rolling windows, and none when the signal law is unknown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-950](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-950.md) | RelExp3 regret needs only local constants | Lattimore and Szepesvári (2019), [LIT-1524](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1524.md), read in [NOTE-1162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1162.md). For the class of games Bartók (2013) studied, the leading constant of the √n regret depends only on K_loc, F and log K, asymptotically. It is the first such result against adversaries. The constant reached before the asymptotics set in still depends on large game constants. It is a bound for one algorithm in a sub-class of the easy games, not a characterisation of the constant. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-957](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-957.md) v2 | Importance weighting estimates unseen signals | Kwon and Perchet (2017), [LIT-1526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1526.md), read in [NOTE-1159](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1159.md). Under decision-dependent partial monitoring, information about a decision's signal comes only from playing it, and its unbiased estimate costs variance inversely proportional to the probability of playing it. A floor is how the algorithm keeps that finite. That the floor is necessary in general is supported by the matching lower bound, not shown here. Nothing here says what floor a non-learning system should keep. | Active |
| [THEORY-961](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-961.md) v2 | Degenerate actions don't create neighbour pairs | Lattimore and Szepesvári (2019), [LIT-1524](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1524.md), read in [NOTE-1162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1162.md), on Bartók et al. (2014), [LIT-1528](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1528.md). Of actions optimal only on a boundary: "Although these actions are never uniquely optimal, they can be informative". They enter the classification only through the neighbourhood set N_ab. Bartók et al.'s lower-bound proof chose the separating direction in the kernel of the two neighbours' signals alone. With such an action informative, that direction can be told apart cheaply. The fix is to take it in the kernel of every action in N_ab, which the definition of local observability already provides. It says what such actions contribute, not how often an algorithm must play them. | Active |
| [THEORY-962](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-962.md) v4 | Local observability fixes learnable comparisons | Bartók, Foster, Pál, Rakhlin and Szepesvári (2014), [LIT-1528](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1528.md), read in [NOTE-1164](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1164.md). Observability in partial monitoring is a linear-algebra condition on the loss and signal matrices: a comparison is learnable from some actions exactly when its loss difference is in the span of their signal row spaces. Global and local observability are the two choices of D the classification uses. It says what can be estimated, not how fast; the rates are [THEORY-964](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-964.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-963](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-963.md) v2 | Partial-monitoring regret has four classes | Lattimore and Szepesvári (2019), [LIT-1524](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1524.md), read in [NOTE-1162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1162.md), completing Bartók et al. (2014), [LIT-1528](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1528.md). The four classes, trivial, easy, hard and hopeless, now cover every finite game. Two things change from Bartók et al.'s statement: the adversarial half no longer excludes degenerate and duplicate actions, and the trivial class is "no pair of neighbouring actions", not "one non-dominated action", which misplaces games whose extra actions are degenerate or duplicates. It classifies the best policy in a fixed, known game, up to game-dependent constants. It does not cover a learner barred from some actions, feedback that changes during play, or adaptive adversaries. | Active |
| [THEORY-964](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-964.md) v3 | Partial monitoring has four regret rates | Bartók, Foster, Pál, Rakhlin and Szepesvári (2014), [LIT-1528](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1528.md), read in [NOTE-1164](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1164.md). Four classes, trivial, easy, hard and hopeless, with conditions checkable from the matrices before play. It classifies the best policy for a fixed, known game. It does not cover a policy that is barred from some actions, a feedback structure that changes during play, or finite-horizon constants, and its adversarial half excludes degenerate games. | Superseded — by [THEORY-963](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-963.md) |
| [THEORY-967](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-967.md) | Attention heads are repurposed during training | Wang, Hoogland, van Wingerden, Furman and Murfet (2024), [LIT-1535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1535.md), read in [NOTE-1188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1188.md). "Heads 0:1, 0:4, 0:7 ultimately become the two previous-token heads and (layer 0) Dyck head respectively. However, these heads appear to start out as simple n-gram heads." Layer-0 multigram heads lose information about simple n-grams from stage LM3, as path patching and composition scores show them coming to feed layer-1 bracket-matching heads. The "ago" n-gram moves from head 0:0 to head 1:0. Whether the late roles are built from the early ones, or merely follow them in time, is not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-973](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-973.md) v2 | Induction heads cause abrupt in-context learning | Olsson et al. (2022), [LIT-1538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1538.md), read in [NOTE-1173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1173.md): Arguments 1–3 for the small attention-only series, with the smeared-key models. The score jumps from under 0.15 to about 0.4 nats in the window where induction heads form, pattern-preserving ablation of the induction heads removes nearly all of it to the end of training, and an architecture that lets one layer express induction moves the jump. It says nothing causal about models with MLPs or large models, and nothing about few-shot task learning, which the score does not measure. | Active |
| [THEORY-975](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-975.md) v2 | Head learning coefficients cluster by function | Wang, Hoogland, van Wingerden, Furman and Murfet (2024), [LIT-1535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1535.md), read in [NOTE-1188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1188.md): §4.1, Figs. 1–2 and 11, appendices B, F.5 and G. Per-head curves of how degenerate the loss is in that head's weights separate the heads by what they end up doing, and the separation is in the curves' shapes over training, not only their end values. It is one small model, cluster counts chosen by eye, and estimates whose ordering, not value, the authors trust. It does not show that the coefficient predicts a head's type before the type is visible. | Active |
| [THEORY-981](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-981.md) v2 | Symmetry fixes a subspace gradient descent keeps | Musat et al. (2026), [LIT-1530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1530.md), read in [NOTE-1177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1177.md). Symmetries of the data confine population gradient descent to the weights those symmetries fix; for their task class and idealized architecture this is a subspace whose coordinates are interpretable head actions. It does not say the subspace is attractive (the paper proves only invariance), and it does not cover minibatch noise beyond expectation, learnable value maps (a sketch in the paper), or adaptive optimizers, which keep it only when the basis is coordinate-aligned. | Active |
| [THEORY-990](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-990.md) v2 | Induction heads drive most in-context learning | Olsson et al. (2022), [LIT-1538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1538.md), read in [NOTE-1173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1173.md). The paper's thesis: circuits with the induction head's mechanism, matching "[A*][B*] … [A] → [B], where A* ≈ A and B* ≈ B are similar in some space", "implement most in-context learning in large models". For large models the authors grade their own evidence correlational (Argument 1), weakly interventional (Argument 2), plausibility (Argument 4) and analogy (Argument 6). Their strongest alternative is that other composition heads, formed in the same window, carry more of it above some size. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-997](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-997.md) | Fine-tuning rewires existing circuits | Wang et al. (2025), [LIT-1539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1539.md), read in [NOTE-1183](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1183.md). Their EAP-IG circuits (top 5% of edges) change edges 2.8–4.3 times as much as nodes over LoRA fine-tuning on five arithmetic tasks. A record simulation shows that a fixed edge budget on a transformer-sized graph gives the same contrast when only edge-level noise is resampled, so the counts do not yet show reorganization. Fine-tuning only, one model for most results, arithmetic only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1001.md) | Circuits sharing units cooperate; rivals compete | Musat et al. (2026), [LIT-1530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1530.md), read in [NOTE-1177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1177.md). In projected SGD training of a three-layer single-head attention-only transformer on in-context bigrams, three induction circuits are possible, and the winner depends on initial strengths outside the winner itself. The authors explain the pattern by cooperation through a shared unit and competition for layers. The evidence is one scan over two initial strengths with every other coordinate zeroed, in projected training. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1009.md) v2 | In-weights circuit scales the induction gradient | Musat et al. (2026), [LIT-1530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1530.md), read in [NOTE-1177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1177.md). A memorized shortcut that solves part of the data removes the in-context circuit's gradient on that part and leaves the rest. It is a theorem in an idealized model under a disjointness assumption (A4) that the paper's own sampler violates, at a cost it states. It does not say the observed order in the paper's one run is due to it: there fr = 0.9 and the factor is 0.9. | Active |
| [THEORY-1057](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1057.md) | Backprop is functoriality of lens semantics | Spivak (2026), [LIT-1649](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1649.md), read in [NOTE-1225](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1225.md) from arXiv v2. Lens internalization (Corollary 3.3.4) and an integrator give operad functors ArrSm → PC (Theorem 4.3.6, Corollary 6.4.1). Under the configuration integrator the state update is q ↦ q − ♯_q(ξ_Q), with ξ_Q the Q*-component of the sum in (58); a parameterized map wired to a loss gives gradient descent (76), a weight-only potential gives weight decay (Proposition 7.2.3), and an inverse-Hessian response gives Newton's method (67). Active as mathematics. Per datum, deterministic, explicit-Euler; Adam and momentum are conjectures. | Active |
| [THEORY-1199](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1199.md) | Skill games have a spinning-top geometry | Czarnecki et al.'s hypothesis ([LIT-1504](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1504.md), read in [NOTE-1146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1146.md)), filed beside [THEORY-930](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-930.md) when the status review of 2026-10-30 narrowed and promoted that entry under [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). The paper's body says it does not prove that real games have this geometry; its evidence is [THEORY-930](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-930.md)'s sampled profiles, whose shape the sampler and the maximum-entropy equilibrium help set. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1218](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1218.md) | MoE gate collapse is self-reinforcing | The authors' explanation in Shazeer et al. (2017), [LIT-1507](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1507.md), p. 5, stated and not tested. Kept here when the twenty-second status review promoted [THEORY-927](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-927.md) as the report ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1231.md) | Mean-field Q-learning reduces to two-body terms | The wide form of Yang et al. (2018), [LIT-1512](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1512.md), kept here when the twenty-fourth status review narrowed [THEORY-945](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-945.md) to the re-derived expansion and to what the paper states and ran, and promoted it ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper asserts that mean field Q-learning converges to the Nash Q-value under its assumptions, and that it makes many-agent learning tractable. Its proof does not reconcile a high-temperature contraction with a greedy limit, and its many-agent evidence is one task at two sizes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1234.md) | Replicator model fits FAQ, not plain Q-learning | The wide form of Kaisers & Tuyls (AAMAS 2010), [LIT-1511](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1511.md), kept here when the twenty-fourth status review narrowed [THEORY-932](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-932.md) to what the derivation proves and what their three games showed, and promoted it ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper asserts that the model is exact for frequency-adjusted Q-learning and that Q-learning departs from it depending on initialization. Its plots are three games, one temperature, compared by eye. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1249](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1249.md) | Deep-goal competence determines the world model | Richens, Abel, Bellot and Everitt (2025), [LIT-1891](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1891.md), Theorems 1 and 2, read in [NOTE-1469](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1469.md). The reduction offers the agent a choice between "at most k successes of a transition in n attempts" and "more than k"; its switch point locates the binomial median. The final bound was re-derived and checked numerically against an adversarial δ-bounded agent. Active: a theorem, checked. It says the transition function is recoverable from the input-output map, not that any component of the agent represents it, and it needs full observation, determinism and the regret bound on every listed goal. | Active |
| [THEORY-1252](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1252.md) v2 | Repeated self-distillation collapses to zero | Mobahi, Farajtabar and Bartlett (2020), [LIT-1895](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1895.md), eqs. 24–37 and §§3.2–4; read in [NOTE-1478](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1478.md), with the paper's illustrative example reproduced from its own sample values. Active for the recurrence, the rising multiplier and collapse, which are elementary and reproduced; the sparsity rate of Theorem 5 is the paper's, proof not checked. It does not show that deep networks behave so, and the amplification depends on holding the error tolerance fixed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1253](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1253.md) | Evidence heat capacity is half parameters or RLCT | LaMont & Wiggins (2019), [LIT-1882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1882.md), read in [NOTE-1481](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1481.md): the learning capacity C = −N²∂_N U and its equipartition values (Table II, eqs. 16–18, 24, 28, 30). Active: the regular entries were checked by differentiation, and the singular case exactly in K = a²b² ([CASE-152](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-152.md)'s model), where C approaches λ = ½ as ½ − 1/log n, not with the O(1/N) error the paper states. The statistical "temperature" is a sample size, so nothing in the dictionary is a physical heat flow. | Active |
| [THEORY-1254](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1254.md) v2 | Uniformly safe controllers forfeit committed value | Saligrama (2026), [LIT-1880](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1880.md), Theorem 1 and its examples, read in [NOTE-1466](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1466.md). Active: a theorem with a short proof, checked. | [THEORY-1255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1255.md) v2 | Constant SGD's stationary law can match posterior | Mandt, Hoffman and Blei (2017, [LIT-1898](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1898.md); first in 2016, [LIT-1899](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1899.md)), read in [NOTE-1475](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1475.md) and [NOTE-1473](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1473.md). Under Gaussian, constant gradient noise BBᵀ, the continuous-time limit and a quadratic loss with positive-definite Hessian A, the stationary covariance solves AΣ + ΣA = (ε/S)BBᵀ; the preconditioner (2S/εN)(BBᵀ)⁻¹ makes it the posterior's A⁻¹/N exactly. Checked numerically. Active as a result about that model. It does not cover singular posteriors, several basins or the search phase, and it relates the optimiser's noise scale to sample size, not training time to sample size. | Active |
| [THEORY-1256](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1256.md) v2 | Confidence-bound control stays safe, nears oracle | Saligrama (2026), [LIT-1880](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1880.md), §5 (Lemma 5, Theorem 2, Corollaries 5–7, §5.6.1), read in [NOTE-1466](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1466.md) with the proofs of Lemma 5 and Theorem 2. Active: a short proof by a Gaussian mixture martingale and Ville's inequality, checked by hand, and an elementary calculation for certainty equivalence. Narrow: a scalar parameter with a known conservative direction, an experiment that returns to a common state, and Gaussian observations. | Active |
| [THEORY-1257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1257.md) v2 | Averaged SGD can match posterior covariance | Mandt, Hoffman and Blei (2017), [LIT-1898](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1898.md), §6 and App. G, read in [NOTE-1475](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1475.md). In their OU model, the mean of T stationary iterates at batch S has covariance A⁻¹BBᵀA⁻¹/(TS) to leading order in 1/(Tελ), whatever the step size or constant preconditioner; under a well-specified regular model (BBᵀ = A) that is A⁻¹/(TS), the Gaussian posterior's covariance for TS observations. Checked against the exact discrete covariance. It is the one place the paper ties examples processed to a sample size, and it is about spread in one basin after equilibration, not about which region dominates. | Active |
| [THEORY-1258](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1258.md) v2 | Fractional SGD model is tempered only regionally | Hennick and De Baerdemacker (2025; ICLR 2026), [LIT-1879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1879.md), read in [NOTE-1467](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1467.md). Their Lemma 3.3 and Corollary 3.2 show that where a scalar effective diffusion D_ξ is constant, the steady state is exp(−L_m/D_ξ), the posterior at effective sample size 1/D_ξ. That is a temperature, and inside such a region it leaves no room for an accessibility correction. Across regions their own equation's zero-flux state is ∝ exp(−∫∇L/D), set by D along the paths between regions; checked on a double well. Active: the algebra and the counterexample are elementary and checked. It does not say SGD is far from Bayesian across regions, only that the paper does not show it is close. | Active |

| [THEORY-1275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1275.md) v2 | SGD transitions only partly match the posterior | Chen, Lau, Mendel, Wei and Murfet (2023), [LIT-1894](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1894.md), read in [NOTE-1462](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1462.md). Their Bayesian antecedent hypothesis is one-way: training's transitions have Bayesian counterparts. From their numbers the antecedents of the chain 4⁺⁺⁻ → 4⁺ → 5 → 5⁺ fall at n ≈ 190, 370 and 1,600–2,500, rising with training. But the posterior's transition 5 → 6 at n ≈ 600 was not seen in training, and SGD on 1000 samples ends at the 5-gon, a 4-gon variant or the 5⁺-gon, none of which the posterior at n = 1000 favours; it favours the 6-gon. The rising order holds at the point estimates, not across the estimates' spread. One model, one SGD setting, estimated learning coefficients; the computation was re-run by a second checker on 2026-11-06 (scratch/formal/tms_critical_sizes_check.py). | Active |

| [THEORY-2006](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2006.md) | Longer pre-training can worsen fine-tuned models | From the reading of [LIT-2829](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2829.md) in [NOTE-2119](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2119.md). Springer, Goyal, Wen, Kumar, Yue, Malladi, Neubig and Raghunathan (2025), arXiv 2503.19206. They name "catastrophic overtraining": past an inflection point, longer pre-training leaves a worse model after instruction or multimodal fine- tuning even though the base model keeps improving (OLMo-1B at 3T against 2.3T tokens; not seen at 7B up to 3T). In controlled small models and a deep-linear theory, they trace it to "progressive sensitivity": a fine- tune of fixed size destroys more pre-trained capability the longer the model was pre-trained. The cost shows up mostly as forgetting caused by the acquisition, and the new task itself gets worse only in some settings. It is here as the prime empirical case for overconsolidation ([CLAIM-758](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-758.md)) and the Pythia study ([CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md)), which it qualifies: the case is mainly about forgetting under modification, not a higher budget to acquire. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |

Sun, Wang, Liu, Miller, Efros and Hardt (2020), ICML 2020, arXiv 1909.13231. The paper that named test-time training: before predicting, a jointly trained network fine-tunes its shared features on a self-supervised task (rotation prediction) built from the single unlabeled test image, then discards the update or, in the online version, keeps it for the next image. It improves classification under corruption, video and CIFAR-10.1 shifts without hurting the original test set, and the gain tracks the alignment of the two tasks' gradients (proved for convex losses). Here because the owner raised test-time training at U26: its discarded and kept updates are the two sides of [CLAIM-118](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-118.md), and its appendix prices the work moved to test time ([QUESTION-095](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-095.md)). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |

Biderman, Schoelkopf, Anthony, Bradley, O'Brien and others (2023), ICML 2023, arXiv 2304.01373. Pythia is eight decoder-only language models, 70M to 12B parameters, each trained once on the Pile and once on a deduplicated Pile (about 1.5 epochs) in one fixed data order, with 154 public checkpoints per model (step 0, ten log-spaced early steps, every 1,000 steps to 143,000) and tools to reconstruct the batches seen up to each; one run per size, cosine learning-rate decay to a tenth of peak. Its case studies find training order has little effect on memorization and a term-frequency effect on few-shot accuracy that appears only late and only at 2.8B and above. Here because it is the testbed of [CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md), whose named models (70M- and 160M-deduped) and checkpoints exist as described, and because many THEORY entries use its models without an entry for the suite. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2015](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2015.md) | Pre-training loss misranks fine-tuned models | From the reading of [LIT-2820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2820.md) in [NOTE-2125](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2125.md). Han, Bordt, Zhang and Kakade (2026), arXiv 2602.11137, ICML 2026. They pre-train Llama-2 and OLMo-2 models (0.5B-4B, at 20 and 140 tokens per parameter) across AdamW weight decay values, then fine-tune on twelve tasks. Weight decay above the default 0.1 gives better fine-tuned performance even where it worsens pre-training loss (OLMo-2-1B at 140 tokens per parameter), so pre-training loss does not rank models by what they become. Plasticity is measured only as the fine-tuned score on the target task, and forgetting is not measured. It is here as a preventive training regime for overconsolidation ([CLAIM-758](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-758.md)) and an arm of [CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md), and it is the clearest case for [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md)'s point that present capability does not rank later capability. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2019.md) | First-order Reptile matches MAML | From the reading of [LIT-2791](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2791.md) in [NOTE-2102](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2102.md). Nichol, Achiam and Schulman (2018), OpenAI, arXiv 1803.02999. Reptile meta-learns an initialization by repeatedly training on a sampled task and moving the initialization toward the result; it matches MAML on few-shot Omniglot and Mini-ImageNet with first-order gradients only, and a Taylor expansion shows its update, like MAML's, is joint training plus a term rewarding generalization between mini-batches of one task, a term that grows with step size and inner steps and is absent at one step. The authors suggest plain SGD does part of this already and that joint training plus fine-tuning stays a strong baseline; their RL results were negative. Here because A54 proposed it as the meta-trained arm of CASE- tmphsr99: the reading supports it as a cheap arm, with joint training on the same tasks as its control and the inner budget k fixed. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2020](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2020.md) | Meta-learned sparse features curb forgetting | From the reading of [LIT-2828](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2828.md) in [NOTE-2106](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2106.md). Javed and White (2019), arXiv 1905.12588, NeurIPS 2019. OML meta-trains a representation by differentiating through online SGD on correlated streams, then freezes it beneath a small predictor that learns online. On Incremental Sine Waves and Split-Omniglot this gives far less forgetting than pre- trained or sparse representations, and learning faster than approximate IID training. The representation turns out highly sparse with no dead units. It is here because A54 named it for representations meta-trained against forgetting, bearing on overconsolidation ([CLAIM-758](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-758.md)). It bears mostly on forgetting: it secures retention and fast acquisition together by freezing the representation, and it says nothing on plasticity over long training. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2023.md) | Learned adaptation routing doubles utility | From the reading of [LIT-2806](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2806.md) in [NOTE-2084](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2084.md). Lu and Kankanhalli (2026), arXiv 2610.12002. Five test-time-training methods become tools that produce reusable LoRA skills over a frozen backbone, and a policy trained by distillation and GRPO decides per query whether to answer directly, reuse a skill or build one, on utility gain minus a compute penalty. On a benchmark deliberately enriched for queries where adaptation helps, it raises Qwen2.5-7B's verified utility from 0.256 to 0.510, cuts adaptation compute by about 30% under a moderate penalty without losing utility, and amortizes skill construction through reuse (61 of 100 reuses help, 1 harms). Here because A58 cited it for learning when to update: its rule, build when gain amortized over expected reuse covers the compute, is [QUESTION-095](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-095.md)'s trade and [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s criterion for parameter skills. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2025](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2025.md) | MAML works by feature reuse, not adaptation | From the reading of [LIT-2822](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2822.md) in [NOTE-2131](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2131.md). Raghu, Raghu, Bengio and Vinyals (2019), arXiv 1909.09157, ICLR 2020. On standard few-shot benchmarks, freezing MAML's network body at test time barely changes accuracy, and body representations hardly move during adaptation (CCA above 0.9). MAML's success is therefore "feature reuse", not "rapid learning", and ANIL, which adapts only the head, matches MAML. It is here because A54 used it to separate reusable structure from the capacity to acquire structure, a clause of [CLAIM-758](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-758.md). The paper supports that distinction between routes to fast adaptation but does not measure acquisition capacity over training or forgetting. It also warns that a low adaptation budget can measure reuse rather than plasticity ([CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md)). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2027.md) | Backprop loses plasticity over many tasks | From the reading of [LIT-2810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2810.md) in [NOTE-2137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2137.md). Dohare, Hernandez- Garcia, Rahman, Mahmood and Sutton (2023), arXiv 2306.13812 (v3, "Maintaining Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning"), published with Lan as "Loss of plasticity in deep continual learning", Nature 632, 768-774 (2024), open access. On long sequences of new tasks (Continual ImageNet, Permuted MNIST, class-incremental CIFAR-100, ant locomotion with PPO), standard deep learning gradually loses the ability to learn new tasks, which the authors keep distinct from forgetting. On ImageNet it falls to about a linear network, and on CIFAR-100 below retraining from scratch with old classes still trained. Small weights with continual injection of randomness (Shrink and Perturb, and their continual backpropagation) maintain plasticity, but all are applied from the start, and none is tested as a late rescue. It is here for overconsolidation (CLAIM-758) beside [THEORY-1353](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1353.md), whose depletion reading it fits: plasticity is lost while the network keeps practising on varied tasks. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2031.md) | Chaotic deep nets grow curvature exponentially | From the reading of [LIT-2842](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2842.md) in [NOTE-2099](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2099.md). The mean-field theory Schoenholz and colleagues build on. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2033](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2033.md) | Contrastive loss splits into alignment, uniformity | From the reading of [LIT-2819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2819.md) in [NOTE-2113](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2113.md). Wang, Isola (2020), ICML 2020 (PMLR 119), arXiv 2005.10242. As the number of negatives grows, the normalized InfoNCE loss on the unit hypersphere converges to an alignment term, minimized exactly when both members of every positive pair share a feature, plus a uniformity term, minimized by a uniform distribution of features on the sphere. On a finite augmented dataset the two optima cannot both be met, and weighting alignment far above uniformity maps every input to one vector. Across several hundred encoders, low alignment and uniformity losses go with good downstream accuracy, and optimizing them directly matches or beats the contrastive loss. Here because A27 used it for how self-supervised learning contracts some distinctions and keeps others ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19, [CLAIM-762](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-762.md)). It supports that split but is not spectral and says nothing of the classes kept. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2034](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2034.md) | Meta-learning is optimizing a meta-objective | From the reading of [LIT-2796](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2796.md) in [NOTE-2108](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2108.md). Hospedales, Antoniou, Micaelli and Storkey (2020), arXiv 2004.05439, a survey of meta-learning in neural networks. It defines meta-learning as end-to-end optimization of an explicit meta-objective over many learning episodes "to improve its future learning performance", orders methods by what is meta- learned, how and for what objective, and lists meta-overfitting, generalization to task distributions other than the training one, and the lack of task families as open problems. Here because the owner asked at U24 for prior meta-learning literature and A54 named this survey: it confirms that meta-learning's objective targets future learning, as [QUESTION-495](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-495.md) and [CLAIM-758](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-758.md) say, and that every such objective presupposes a declared task family. Skimmed (taxonomy, formalization, meta-objectives, continual learning, challenges); read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2035](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2035.md) | Abstract rules follow data diversity, not design | Li and Webb ([LIT-2830](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2830.md)), read in [NOTE-2094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2094.md). The flip rate of a mean-difference rule vector is 0% at vocabulary 50, 5% at 100 and close to 100% from 500; at vocabulary 100 it goes from 5% with 2 rules to 95% with 10, and from 98% to near 0% as role-token bias rises, while every model still generalizes in distribution. At vocabularies of 100 or less the 12-layer model first solves the task without it and acquires it long after convergence. Ablated transformers and a pure MLP reach 90–100% at vocabulary 10k. The mechanism in the MLP is unidentified, and there is no random-network control. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2037.md) | Meta-training improves in-context learning | From the reading of [LIT-2803](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2803.md) in [NOTE-2104](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2104.md). Min, Lewis, Zettlemoyer and Hajishirzi (2021; arXiv 2110.15943, v2 May 2022) fine- tune GPT-2 Large on 142 NLP datasets presented as few-shot episodes, training it to predict the last example's output from the k before it. On 52 held-out target tasks, with no parameter updates, the meta-trained model beats plain in-context learning and multi-task zero-shot transfer in most of seven splits. The gains are largest on targets unlike the training tasks, and it matches a model 8x larger. Fine-tuning after meta-training remains better, and without meaningful label words every model falls near chance unless meta-trained on remapped labels. Here because A54 named it where meta-learning and in-context learning meet. It is the plainest case of outer training improving the interpreter so that it uses the signal better ([CLAIM-118](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-118.md)), and of the meta-learning arm of [CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2041](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2041.md) v2 | Trainable depth is set by a correlation scale | From the reading of [LIT-2825](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2825.md) in [NOTE-2101](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2101.md). Schoenholz, Gilmer, Ganguli and Sohl-Dickstein (2017), ICLR 2017, arXiv 1611.01232. In the mean-field theory of wide random networks with bounded activations, the correlation between two inputs decays to its limit over a depth scale ξc that diverges only at the order-to-chaos transition; gradients vanish or explode over the same scale on either side, and in experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 networks train only when their depth is below about 6ξc, so very deep networks train only near criticality, and dropout, which removes the transition, caps trainable depth. Here because A15 set it against domain walls as a way of keeping information through depth: it is the fine-tuned edge-of-chaos route that the read stand-in LIT- tmpyahtz ([THEORY-2051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2051.md)) claims to avoid over a whole symmetry-broken phase. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2045](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2045.md) | Active learning usually but not reliably helps | From the reading of [LIT-2799](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2799.md) in [NOTE-2118](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2118.md). Settles (2009; revised 26 January 2010), Active Learning Literature Survey, Computer Sciences Technical Report 1648, University of Wisconsin–Madison, https://burrsettles.com/pub/settles.activelearning.pdf. The standard survey of active learning: query scenarios, query strategies (uncertainty sampling, query-by-committee, expected error reduction, variance reduction), and the evidence for them. It also covers practical issues such as variable labelling costs, unknown model classes and stopping criteria. It reports that active learning usually saves labels but can fail: the data are biased toward the model that chose them, cost-blind selection can do no better than random, and greedy guarantees need submodularity, which active-learning criteria generally lack. Here because the owner said at U30 that the exchange was entering active- learning territory. It bears on [CLAIM-572](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-572.md)'s greedy-stopping result and on the feedback premise of [QUESTION-494](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-494.md). Read in its NOTE (skimmed). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2046](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2046.md) | MAML trains initializations for fast adaptation | From the reading of [LIT-2816](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2816.md) in [NOTE-2090](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2090.md). Finn, Abbeel and Levine (2017), ICML 2017, arXiv 1703.03400. MAML trains a network's initial parameters on the loss after one or a few gradient steps on each task drawn from a declared task distribution, so that the model is, in the authors' words, "easy to fine-tune"; on sinusoid regression, few- shot Omniglot and MiniImagenet and goal-conditioned RL it adapts from a handful of examples where joint pretraining on the same tasks does not. Here because its objective already targets future adaptability, the disclaimer [CLAIM-758](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-758.md) and [QUESTION-495](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-495.md) carry: the reading confirms it, for a declared task distribution and a declared adaptation budget only. It also gives an empirical instance of [CLAIM-756](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-756.md), an initialization ranked below joint training on present loss and above it once adaptation is counted. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2050.md) | ICL transformers act like standard estimators | From the reading of [LIT-2811](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2811.md) in [NOTE-2121](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2121.md). Akyürek, Schuurmans, Andreas, Ma and Zhou (ICLR 2023; arXiv 2211.15661) prove that a transformer can implement one gradient-descent step or one ridge- regression update on in-context examples. They then show that transformers trained on in-context linear regression behave like standard estimators chosen by capacity: one gradient step at one layer (poorly), ridge at two to four layers, least squares at eight or more. With label noise the high-capacity learners match the Bayes-optimal ridge predictor. Probes recover the moment vector and least-squares weights from hidden states, but nonlinearly, unlike the constructions. Here because A56 cited it beside Garg et al. for in-context learning as a learned learner. It measures [THEORY-169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-169.md)'s caution that trained transformers are not shown to do gradient descent, and it is a case of [CLAIM-118](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-118.md)'s split. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2051.md) | Equivariant symmetry-broken phase trains deep | Iqbal, Keller, Song, Miyato and Welling ([LIT-2840](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2840.md)), read in [NOTE-2126](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2126.md). A mean-field analysis gives the transition and the protected Jacobian component; 100-layer equivariant MLPs train across the broken phase; generic networks show the same order parameter with no performance gain. Defects (U(1) vortices) form in a convolutional RNN but their use is not shown. A stand-in for the thesis of [LIT-2787](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2787.md), the owner's U6 example. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2052.md) | Transformers learn function classes in context | From the reading of [LIT-2839](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2839.md) in [NOTE-2103](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2103.md). Garg, Tsipras, Liang and Valiant (2022; arXiv 2208.01066, v3 Aug 2023) define in-context learning of a function class as a property of a fixed model and train small transformers from scratch to achieve it. On unseen 20-dimensional linear functions the trained model matches least squares, and it stays close under noisy labels, subspace inputs and mismatched orthants. Trained on sparse linear functions, depth-4 trees or two-layer networks, it nears Lasso, beats greedy tree learning and XGBoost, and matches a gradient-trained network. It is fragile under input scaling and skewed covariance, and the authors leave open what this means for language models. Here because A56 cited it for in-context learning as a learned algorithm. It is the behavioural counterpart to the exact identities of [THEORY-169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-169.md) and a case of [CLAIM-118](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-118.md)'s split between a learned interpreter and a discarded per-sequence fit. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2053](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2053.md) | Label re-keying curbs meta-overfitting | From the reading of [LIT-2817](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2817.md) in [NOTE-2089](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2089.md). They separate memorization overfitting, where the model ignores the support set, from learner overfitting, where the base learner fails on new tasks even when tasks are mutually exclusive, and show that re-keying each task's labels at random (label shuffling for classification, shared noise for regression) improves meta-test performance, on top of Yin et al.'s meta- regularization; Mini-ImageNet MAML rose from 30% to 46%. Here because A54 used it beside Yin et al. ([LIT-2838](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2838.md)) for [CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md): the reading supports the case's held-out task-generating processes, since learner overfitting survives shuffling, and adds two rules, several seeds and pre/post-update accuracy as the diagnostic. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2056](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2056.md) | Meta-learners can memorize, ignoring support data | From the reading of [LIT-2838](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2838.md) in [NOTE-2116](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2116.md).
